title: Modelled writing must be error-free
statement: Text that models what students should write must be free of errors, because students may copy it.
example: One lesson's modelled method lines had comma splices on three pages.
detail: A review of one Grade 3 lesson found comma splices in the annotation lines that model the method on three pages and asked for them to be fixed, because those lines model the method for the child, so the punctuation is copied (`shadow/content-eval/reports/G3-U2-L1-review.md`). That students copy it is the review's reasoning, not a measurement.

evidence.quote: These lines model the method for the child, so the punctuation is copied.
Inspect G3-U1-L6/p19 retell supplied example: it places ship march before Peter escapes, contrary to p10 and p11.
modeled writing is copy, and must be punctuated as publishable prose, because it is the only model of correct writing the child sees.

This is the second punctuation correction on modeled text, after Scout’s modeled answer on Aladdin, which makes it worth a standing rule: modeled writing is copy, and must be punctuated as publishable prose, because it is the only model of correct writing the child sees.
